items.statement: Across published reviews, multifaceted interventions that combine practice feedback with patient-level review raise appropriate anticoagulation more than single-component interventions.
items.rationale: Directly informs the board's choice between proposals; feasible with library support; the leads suggest the contrast exists in the literature.
items.risks: Reviews may define multifaceted differently; overlap may inflate agreement.

items.statement: Few reviews report stroke or major bleeding, so no intervention can be ranked on patient outcomes.
items.rationale: Protects the board from reading prescribing gains as fewer strokes.
items.risks: A null finding about reporting is easy to misread as no effect.

items.statement: Decision aids change decisional quality without changing the proportion prescribed.
items.rationale: Matters for people who declined treatment before.

summary: Three review-level hypotheses; h1 selected, h2 and h3 kept as pre-specified secondary questions.
